methods.summary: A source-bounded study of advertised expectations. We retrieve occupations without an AI keyword requirement, preserve full descriptions privately, and separate explicit role evidence from employer context. This release adds broad automated coding and partial contextual AI review; it does not complete independent human validation.

steps.title: Retrieve and preserve
steps.description: Pin the public OpenJobData source revision. Recover the provider’s full description components, retain source identifiers and text hashes, and collapse conservative same-requisition mirrors.

steps.title: Screen and sample
steps.description: Use documented occupational and US eligibility rules without selecting on AI. Draw from deterministic randomized candidate queues. Keep closed ads and unknown posting dates visible; do not treat first-seen dates as original posting dates.

steps.title: Define and code
steps.description: Maintain operational definitions with inclusion and exclusion examples. Separate AI used in one’s work, AI as the product being built or studied, and enabling others. A mention is not necessarily a requirement, a duty, or hands-on expertise.

steps.title: Audit and retain uncertainty
steps.description: Review proposed evidence in context, including negative and ambiguous cases. Record disagreements and missed matches. Independent human coding and a random negative-case audit are still needed before reporting validated prevalence.

limitations: Source-bounded, English-language retained ads; no probability sample of the US labor market.
Known dates are in 2026, but closed ads and unknown original dates are included. Collection date is not posting date.
Automatic rules can confuse employer AI products with role expectations and can miss implicit terminology.
Review coverage differs by occupation. Map candidate rates, reviewed detections and historical pilot rates are different measures.

The retained baseline includes one design ad with explicit non-US location and nine UXR ads with unresolved or conflicting location evidence. See the corroborated-US sensitivity report; these flags have not been silently removed.
Occupations, employers, seniority and specialties differ. Hybrid roles can occur across cohorts; percentages are not an occupation ranking.
Advertisements show advertised expectations, not observed workplace use, productivity, job displacement or causal change.
